To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IR and GLUT 2 proteins interact on the hepatocyte plasma and endosomal membranes and are internalized together.
IR and GLUT-2 proteins interact on the plasma membrane and that the interaction is insulin-dependent.

IR and GLUT-2 are associated in a fixed ratio in the endosomal and plasma membrane fractions of the hepatocyte, that they form a complex when solubilized and immunoprecipiated from rat liver, and that the association of IR and GLU2 is further confirmed by confocal microscopy and fluorescence-resonance energy-transfer studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of insulin receptor and glucose transport proteins in the hepatocyte membrane.
the role of insulin in the control of hepatic glucose homeostasis and the mechanisms by which insulin exerts its actions.
the regulation of hepatic glucose transport by insulin and the role of the insulin receptor and the glucose transporter 2 in this regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IR and GLUT2 interact and colocalize in a receptor- transporter complex.
the insulin receptor is coupled to a glucose transporter (GLUT2), which is the major glucose transporter in the liver.
IR and GLUT 2 are in a receptor- transporter complex in the hepatocyte membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IR and GLUT-2 proteins are physically coupled in hepatocytes, and that this coupling may be important to the mechanism of insulin-mediated regulation of hepatic glucose transport.
the hepatic glucose transporter GLUT2 is physically associated with the insulin receptor in the hepatocyte plasma and endosomal membranes.
insulin receptor and glucose transporter 2 proteins form a complex on the rat hepatocyte membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the insulin receptor (IR) and GLUT2 form an IR-GLUT2 complex on the hepatocyte membrane.
the insulin receptor and GLUT2 form complexes in the hepatocyte membrane, and this complex may be important in regulating glucose transport.
insulin and GLUT2 form an insulin-transporter complex that is internalized and recycled.
